title: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)

sections.label: AI, autonomous vehicles, bus network
sections.summary: It asks how transport infrastructure will be enhanced for AI and autonomous vehicles, and notes up to $900 million for the bus network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With potential artificial intelligence (AI) and autonomous vehicles coming onstream, how is our transport infrastructure going to be enhanced?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It was announced mid-last year that up to $900 million will be spent over the next eight years to improve the bus network under the Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme.

sections.label: NSC construction, Volocopter air taxis
sections.summary: It asks about NSC construction challenges and 2027 to 2029 completion, and notes Volocopter paused Singapore air taxi services over local funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Conceptualised in 2016, the completed NSC will divert vehicular traffic to the underground expressway tunnel, so the ground-level space can be used for wider footpaths, cycling paths, bus priority lanes and more communal and green spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Besides COVID-19, what challenges has the NSC construction encountered and are we on course to achieve completion by 2027 to 2029?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, it was disappointing to see the announcement by Volocopter in November that a lack of local funding partners has forced them to put the launch of air taxi services in Singapore on hold.

sections.label: MRT reliability and disruptions
sections.summary: It states the MRT system has been reliable and performed above the target, but there had been service disruptions including a severe East West Line one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Although our MRT system has been reliable in general, performing well above the target of one million train-kilometres between delays, there had been service disruptions, including a severe one on the East West Line last year.

sections.label: MRT network size and lines
sections.summary: It states that after 38 years the MRT network spans 250 kilometres, with 143 stations and six lines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Fast forward 38 years, our MRT network now spans 250 kilometres, comprising of 143 stations and six lines.

sections.label: Ageing rail assets, rail workforce
sections.summary: It asks how the Ministry will work with tripartite partners to level up the workforce, given ageing rail assets and new carriages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Given that our rail assets are ageing, that there will be new replacements of carriages coming in and the pressures rail workers put themselves through to adhere to top of class deliverables, how will the Ministry work with tripartite partners to level up our workforce to strengthen rail reliability?

sections.label: LTA technology for rail maintenance
sections.summary: It asks how the LTA intends to use technology, including artificial intelligence, for regular rail maintenance and inspections to pre-emptively address issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: How does the LTA intend to use technology, including artificial intelligence, to establish a robust schedule for regular maintenance and inspections for our rail systems, to pre-emptively identify and address potential issues?

sections.label: Extending JRL to other lines
sections.summary: The speaker urges LTA to consider extending the JRL to connect with the Circle Line and upcoming Cross Island Line.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: To enhance resilience in the West, even with JRL, I urge LTA to consider extending the JRL to connect with the Circle Line and the upcoming Cross Island Line as soon as possible.

sections.label: Rail line feasibility and mode share
sections.summary: The passage asks for an update on feasibility studies for a north and northeast rail line and cites public transport mode share figures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide an update on its feasibility studies for a proposed rail line in the north and northeast regions as outlined in the LTMP 2040?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2019, the LTA reported that they were on track to meet its 2030 target of a 75% public transport mode share for all peak period commutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2016, the public transport mode share for MRT, Light Rail Transit (LRT) and buses was 62%.

sections.label: Monthly travel pass economics
sections.summary: The passage compares average monthly public transport expenditure with the prices of adult and concession monthly travel passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As it is for existing adult monthly travel pass holders, their average expenditure without the pass would be about $140 per month, compared to the price of the pass at $128 per month, just a $12 savings a month, on average, for heavy users of public transport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The average monthly expenditure for adult commuters, on the other hand, is estimated to be only about $45, based on the response to my Parliamentary Question earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even for lower-wage workers who qualify for a monthly concession pass at $96 a month, this is barely economical for average users, without even considering that they already received discounts of up to 25% of adult public transport fares.

sections.label: Hougang Avenue 7 bus service
sections.summary: The passage states that Bus Service 112 is the only full-day bus service serving Hougang Avenue 7.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Chairman, currently, and for many years, there is only one full-day bus service, Bus Service 112 serving Hougang Avenue 7.

sections.label: Hougang Avenue 7 new residents
sections.summary: The passage states that new residents, including Riverfront Residences, increased commuter load and some welcome City Direct Service 676.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Newer residents have moved into Hougang Avenue 7 in the past few years, including the large Riverfront Residences condominium from October 2023 onwards, with 1,472 units, increasing the pre-existing commuter load from residents from the Housing and Development Board (HDB) estate and other condominiums along Hougang Avenue 7.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Some residents welcome the new City Direct Service 676 to the Central Business District from 2 January 2025.

sections.label: No new feeder routes
sections.summary: The Minister replied that no new routes were being introduced for intra-town feeder services due to trade-offs involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister replied that no new routes were being introduced for such intra-town feeder services due to the trade-offs involved.

sections.label: Extension time and distance
sections.summary: The speaker estimates the extension adds three to four minutes and about 500 to 600 metres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Based on my estimation, this extension will only have an added time of between three to four minutes and added distance of about 500 to 600 metres.

sections.label: Autonomous bus trial tender
sections.summary: LTA launched a tender seeking proposals to trial autonomous buses and evaluate autonomous vehicle technology for public bus services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, earlier this year, LTA launched a tender, seeking proposals to trial autonomous buses and to evaluate the feasibility of using autonomous vehicle technology for public bus services.

sections.label: Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme launch
sections.summary: The $900 million Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme promises new bus services, new buses and more staff recruitment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: The launch of the $900 million Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme (BCEP) promises improvements with the introduction of new bus services, the purchase of new buses and the recruitment of more staff.

sections.label: Bus Safety Tripartite Taskforce establishment
sections.summary: A series of public bus accidents last year spurred the establishment of the Bus Safety Tripartite Taskforce in July 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, a series of accidents involving public buses last year spurred the establishment of the Bus Safety Tripartite Taskforce in July 2024.

sections.label: Update on bus safety review
sections.summary: The Member asks for an update on the Bus Safety Tripartite Taskforce review, whether it will finish by first half 2025, and any urgent rectification measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Following my Parliamentary Question last November, can the Ministry provide an update on the review of public bus safety by the Bus Safety Tripartite Taskforce?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Is it on course to complete its review by the first half of 2025, and have there been any urgent rectification measures implemented as a result of the feedback and studies so far?

sections.label: Definitive decibel threshold proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes establishing a definitive decibel threshold of around 60 to 70 decibels above which noise is considered disruptive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: First, we should establish a definitive decibel threshold, perhaps around 60 to 70 decibels, above which noise is considered disruptive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: This level corresponds to normal conversation volume, giving a clear objective benchmark.

sections.label: Empowering transport staff enforcement
sections.summary: Transport staff and station officers must be empowered with legal authority and training to enforce the rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Second, we must empower transport staff and station officers with the legal authority and training to enforce these rules.

sections.label: Proportionate penalty framework
sections.summary: The penalty framework must be proportionate yet impactful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Third, the penalty framework must be proportionate, yet impactful.

sections.label: Signs and force of law
sections.summary: The speaker appreciates reminders to commuters but asks whether these signs have the force of law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: And I appreciate the efforts to remind public transport commuters on the need to be thoughtful and considerate to other commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: However, do these signs have the force of law?

sections.label: Covered linkways to TEL stations
sections.summary: The speaker urges LTA to build covered linkways to train stations concurrently with MRT line construction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: The TEL line has facilitated travel for many residents in my constituency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: However, even though the TEL line has been operational for the last eight months, the covered linkway under the Walk to Ride Scheme, which links residents to the train station are not yet put up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: So, I urge LTA to plan concurrently so that the covered linkways to the train stations are constructed at the same time with the construction of the MRT line.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: In that way, once the MRT line is operational, residents can have a sheltered walkway to the train station when they are using the new MRT line.

sections.label: Sheltered crossings and Friendly Streets
sections.summary: The speaker requests sheltered pedestrian crossings in Kaki Bukit and notes Jalan Kayu residents' delight at Friendly Streets selection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For the past few years also, there has also been an increase in PMA users in my ward due to the ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Hence, Sir, I have been persistent in my request to MOT for sheltered pedestrian crossings in my Kaki Bukit ward, linking the 17 blocks and the nearby bus stop to these two neighbourhood centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, my Jalan Kayu residents at one of our HDB estates, Buangkok Crescent, have been delighted to know that they are one of 10 neighbourhoods in Singapore selected by LTA for the Friendly Streets initiative announced in January this year.

sections.label: Friendly Streets in private estates
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether LTA can consider Friendly Streets along Seletar Road and Jalan Redop for senior safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Given LTA’s intention to extend piloting Friendly Streets to also private estates to ensure safe mobility for seniors living there, can LTA consider: one, Friendly Streets initiative along the main Seletar Road and Jalan Redop, for example, as the gradient of these roads has seen some vehicles speeding through during early mornings, when senior residents come out for morning walks and, in the evenings, when seniors take their after-dinner strolls?

sections.label: LTA pathway width mandate
sections.summary: In 2018, LTA required new pathways to be at least 1.8 metres wide, up from 1.5 metres previously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In 2018, LTA mandated that new pathways are to be at least 1.8 metres wide, up from 1.5 metres previously.

sections.label: Margaret Drive shared pathway width
sections.summary: In Margaret Drive, an adjacent construction has left one shared pathway at only 1.62 metres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In Margaret Drive, for instance, owing to an adjacent construction, one particular shared pathway is now a mere 1.62 metres.

sections.label: New PMA regulations
sections.summary: MOT will implement and enforce new regulations for Personal Mobility Aids.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, MOT will be implementing and enforcing new regulations for Personal Mobility Aids (PMAs).

sections.label: Co-mingling goods and workers
sections.summary: Co-mingling goods and workers at the back of lorries is dangerous and can cause serious injuries and fatalities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, co-mingling goods and workers at the back of lorries is dangerous and can result in serious injuries and even fatalities.

sections.label: Separating goods and passengers
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry can mandate separating goods and passengers when lorries transport workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Can the Ministry mandate the separation of goods and passengers when using lorries to transport workers?

sections.label: Drivers working long hours
sections.summary: Many drivers drive upwards of 14 hours a day to make ends meet.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Many of our drivers have taken to driving upwards of 14 hours in a day to make ends meet.

sections.label: P2P transport review progress
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry can update on the review of the P2P transport industry structure and regulatory framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide an update on the progress of the review of the P2P transport industry structure and regulatory framework?

sections.label: Montreal taxi livery proposal
sections.summary: The passage describes Montreal taxis using removable taxi tops and urges LTA to consider allowing taxis without livery if clearly identifiable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: In Montreal, taxis are allowed to operate with a large removable taxi top, the taxi top can be removed but without livery, allowing them to function as normal cars when not in service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: I urge LTA to consider allowing taxis to operate without livery, provided they remain clearly identifiable, that means, you can see it is a taxi very clearly, through a removable taxi top and perhaps an additional LCD sign.

sections.label: PTP review and falling earnings
sections.summary: The passage states the LTA PTP sector review is ongoing past its scheduled 2024 conclusion, with driver supply exceeding demand and falling fares and earnings since 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, point-to-point (PTP) transport like taxi and ride-hail services provide options for direct journeys.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: It appears that the LTA's PTP sector review is still ongoing, despite being scheduled to conclude by the second quarter of 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: The recent market conditions are that driver supply exceeds demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Therefore, fares and driver earnings have been falling since the start of 2023.

sections.label: Driver platform choice and COE
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry can ensure PTP drivers can choose their platforms, especially with rising COE prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Having regard to the livelihoods of PTP drivers, how can the Ministry ensure that drivers continue to have the ability to choose the platforms that they wish to drive for?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: This is especially so when the COE prices kept going up and the COE in the Open category hit a high of $152,000 in November last year.

sections.label: LTA COE and private hire measures
sections.summary: The passage states LTA injected 20,000 extra COEs and banned private hire cars from transfer out of the scheme within three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: To be fair, LTA has taken measures to manage COE prices by injecting 20,000 extra COEs over the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: Just last month, LTA has also banned private hire cars from being transferred out of the scheme to become passenger cars or transfer them to individuals within three years of its registration.

sections.label: EV battery warranty terms
sections.summary: The passage states most manufacturers set EV battery warranties at eight years or 160,000 kilometres.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: At present, the warranty on EV batteries for most manufacturers is set at eight years, or 160,000 kilometres.

sections.label: EV battery lifespan
sections.summary: With reasonable use, EV batteries could last between 15 and 20 years before needing replacement.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, with reasonable use, EV batteries could last somewhere between 15 and 20 years before requiring replacement.

sections.label: COE duration revision proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes the Ministry consider revising standard COE duration to 16 years, especially after 2030 when pure ICE COEs end.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In summary, I propose that the Ministry consider revision in the standard COE duration to 16 years, especially after 2030, when the pure ICE COEs will no longer be issued.

sections.label: EV Early Adoption Incentive extension
sections.summary: The EV Early Adoption Incentive gives a 45% rebate on the Additional Registration Fee for fully electric cars and taxis, extended until December 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The EV Early Adoption Incentive offering a 45% rebate on the Additional Registration Fee for fully electric cars and taxis, has been extended until December 2025.

sections.label: Electric vehicle forecast for Singapore
sections.summary: Bloomberg's energy research service forecasts 80% of Singapore passenger vehicles will be electric by 2040, but similar data for electric heavy vehicles is not readily available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Bloomberg's energy research service has forecast that 80% of all passenger vehicles in Singapore are expected to be electric by 2040, but similar data for electric heavy vehicles does not seem to be readily available.

sections.label: EV share of new cars
sections.summary: One-third of new passenger cars registered in 2024 are EVs, with momentum continuing in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Chairperson, we are pleased to note that one-third of new passenger cars registered in 2024 are EVs, with momentum continuing in 2025.

sections.label: Slower commercial electric vehicle adoption
sections.summary: Adoption of electric and hybrid commercial vehicles has been slower than private vehicles, especially heavier industrial ones, due to high sunk investment costs, technical constraints, availability and costs of vehicles, certification requirements, and trained manpower.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Ms Poh Li San, you may take your three cuts together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: However, compared to private vehicles, the adoption of electric and hybrid models for commercial vehicles has been slower, especially the heavier ones used for industrial purposes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Reasons include high sunk investment costs, technical and technological constraints, availability and costs of such vehicles, certification requirements and the availability and costs of trained and qualified manpower to operate and maintain newer vehicle models.

sections.label: Changi Airport passenger movement increase
sections.summary: Changi Airport registered an increase of almost 15% for passenger movement last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Last year, Changi Airport registered an increase of almost 15% for passenger movement.

sections.label: Maritime sector growth categories
sections.summary: The maritime sector enjoyed excellent growth last year in vessel arrival tonnage, container throughput and total bunker sales.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Our maritime sector enjoyed excellent growth in various categories last year, including the annual vessel arrival tonnage, container throughput and total bunker sales.

sections.label: Singapore port record performance
sections.summary: Vessel arrival tonnage reached 3.11 billion gross tonnage and container throughput crossed 40 million TEU for the first time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: The annual vessel arrival tonnage in the port of Singapore reached 3.11 billion gross tonnage, while our container throughput from both PSA terminals and Jurong Port crossed 40 million TEU for the first time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: What are the reasons for the record-breaking performance in 2024 and is it projected to continue upwards?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Our long-time competitor, Port Klang, announced investments to double its capacity in April last year.

sections.label: Port challenges and competitiveness
sections.summary: The member asks how the Ministry ensures competitiveness amid regional competition while attracting workers to the maritime sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: I am heartened to see that we are building on our digitalisation and talent development efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: But there will also be new challenges as we continue to move all port operations to Tuas by 2027, construct "Long Island" and decarbonise our maritime sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: So, Mdm Chair, I would like to ask, how is the Ministry ensuring that we continue to remain competitive amidst fierce competition in the region and, at the same time, pull in more workers, or our own Singaporeans, to be attracted to the maritime sector as well?

sections.label: Maritime talent pipeline and collaborations
sections.summary: The member requests an update on collaborations with Institutions of Higher Learning offering shipping and maritime programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To ensure that Singapore remains a global leader in maritime excellence, we must prioritise building a robust pipeline of talent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also request the Ministry to give this House an update on the collaborations with various Institutions of Higher Learning, which offer programmes related to shipping and the maritime sector, and the scale and extent to which it is working with these institutions, to instill the importance of lifelong learning for staff in the maritime sector.

sections.label: Bunkering alternative fuels safety
sections.summary: The member asks for an update on steps to safely scale up bunkering of alternative fuels such as LNG, biofuels and ammonia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister for Transport to give us an update on the steps Singapore is taking to ensure that the country can scale up the bunkering of alternative fuels safely?

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What are some of the safety guidelines, protocols and regulations in place and how well-prepared are the staff to ensure that the processes take place safely in the handling, storage and transportation of alternative fuels, such as LNG, biofuels and ammonia?

sections.label: Circle Line and MRT line openings
sections.summary: The Circle Line loop closes by mid-next year, and Thomson-East Coast Line Stage 5 and Downtown Line Stage 3 Extension open in second half of 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: By the middle of next year, we will close the loop for the Circle Line, by connecting HarbourFront station to Marina Bay station via three new stations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In the second half of 2026, we will open Thomson-East Coast Line Stage 5 and Downtown Line Stage 3 Extension, linking these two MRT lines.

sections.label: Jurong Region Line extension phases
sections.summary: The WCE proceeds in two phases, extending the Jurong Region Line to West Coast station by late 2030s and Kent Ridge station by early 2040s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Government plans to proceed with the WCE in two phases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The first phase will extend the Jurong Region Line from Pandan Reservoir station to connect with the Cross Island Line at West Coast station by the late 2030s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Under the second phase, our current plan is to further extend the Jurong Region Line from West Coast station to connect with the Circle Line at Kent Ridge station by the early 2040s.

sections.label: Two new MRT lines feasibility
sections.summary: If studies confirm feasibility, two new MRT lines are expected to be completed in phases from the 2040s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If studies confirm that these two new MRT lines are feasible, we expect to complete them in phases from the 2040s.

sections.label: Additional $1 billion rail investment
sections.summary: The Government intends to invest up to an additional $1 billion over the next five years to strengthen rail capabilities and scale up technology adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: To further support these efforts, the Government intends to invest up to an additional $1 billion over the next five years to further strengthen our rail capabilities and scale up technology adoption.

sections.label: LTA asset maintenance decisions
sections.summary: LTA will determine based on each asset's condition whether maintenance is stepped up, the asset is replaced early, or its service life is extended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: LTA will determine, based on the condition of each asset, whether maintenance needs to be stepped up by our operators so that the asset can continue to run until the end of its service life, or whether the asset needs to be replaced early, or if it can have its service life extended.

sections.label: Bus network improvements and expansion
sections.summary: LTA plans 15 more bus services in 2025 and about 20 kilometres of new bus lanes this year, after introducing 10 and enhancing 36 services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Moving to buses, we will continue to improve our public bus network, to provide residents with convenient first- and last-mile access to the rail network, and to amenities in their towns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So far, we have introduced 10 new services and enhanced 36 services to improve capacity and connectivity for residents in Yishun, Tengah, Hougang, as well as Mr Gan's residents in Fernvale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: LTA plans to introduce another 15 more bus services in 2025 across different towns, including Punggol, Bidadari, Yew Tee and Tampines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: LTA will add about 20 kilometres of new bus lanes this year, and more to follow in the coming years.

sections.label: Yishun MRT pilot project
sections.summary: Yishun station, an older MRT station expected to get busier with surrounding developments, will be the pilot project for this programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Yishun station, one of our older MRT stations in Singapore, which is expected to become even busier with surrounding developments, will be the pilot project for this programme.

sections.label: Three integrated air-conditioned interchanges
sections.summary: Three integrated air-conditioned interchanges will open at Woodleigh, Pasir Ris and Punggol Coast in the coming months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: In the coming months, we will open three integrated air-conditioned interchanges at Woodleigh, Pasir Ris and Punggol Coast.

sections.label: West Coast Extension Line phases
sections.summary: The West Coast Extension Line will be implemented in two phases, extending the Jurong Region Line to interchange with the Cross-Island Line and Circle Line.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Chairman, we will implement the West Coast Extension Line in two phases: phase one will extend the Jurong Region Line to interchange with the Cross-Island Line at West Coast station while phase two will extend the Jurong Region Line to interchange with the Circle Line.

sections.label: Bus services and line completion
sections.summary: The lines are expected to be completed in phases from the 2040s, and around 15 new bus services are planned across several areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If feasible, we expect that these lines to be completed in phases from the 2040s, benefitting more than 400,000 households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Last year, we invested close to an additional $1 billion on the Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme (BCEP).

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: In this coming year, we plan to introduce around 15 new services across Punggol, Bidadari, Yew Tee and Tampines and other such areas to benefit more residents.

sections.label: Changi passenger movements recovery
sections.summary: For the 12 months ending February 2025, Changi saw 68.4 million passenger movements, a full recovery over pre-COVID-19 levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For the 12 months ending February 2025, Changi saw 68.4 million passenger movements, representing a full recovery over pre-COVID-19 levels.

sections.label: Terminal 5 groundbreaking and capacity
sections.summary: Ground will be broken for Terminal 5 in a few months, increasing Changi's capacity by 50 million passengers per annum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As an international business centre and a global air hub, Singapore is well-placed to capture these opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We will break ground for Terminal 5 (T5) in a few months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: T5 will increase Changi’s capacity by 50 million passengers per annum, on top of the current 90 million passengers per annum.

sections.label: CAAS aviation funding commitment
sections.summary: CAAS will commit $1 billion over five years to catalyse action and partnership in four areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) will commit $1 billion over the next five years to catalyse action and partnership in these four areas.

sections.label: Singapore city links network
sections.summary: Singapore aims to grow from over 160 to over 200 city links by the mid-2030s to anchor itself as a global node.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Singapore’s current network of over 160 city links connect us with the world and this is a key enabler for our economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We aim to build a larger network of over 200 city links by the mid-2030s, to anchor Singapore as a key global node.

sections.label: Ten-year aviation technology roadmap
sections.summary: CAAS will work with industry and researchers on a 10-year technology roadmap for operational aviation capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: CAAS will work with the industry and the research community to develop a 10-year technology roadmap to guide technology planning and to translate research and development into operational capabilities that can be deployed across the aviation ecosystem.

sections.label: Changi handling capacity increase
sections.summary: Changi's handling capacity will rise from 3.0 to 5.4 million tonnes per annum in the mid-2030s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: In the mid-2030s, Changi’s handling capacity will increase from 3.0 million to 5.4 million tonnes per annum with the opening of the Changi East Industrial Zone.

sections.label: SATS air freight upgrade
sections.summary: SATS plans to invest $100 million over two years, raising cargo capacity from 2.3 to three million tonnes per annum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Changi Airport’s largest cargo handler, SATS, has plans to invest $100 million over the next two years to upgrade its existing air freight terminals at the Changi Airfreight Centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: With this, SATS’ cargo handling capacity will increase by 30%, from 2.3 million tonnes to three million tonnes per annum, and ensure it has sufficient capacity to support growing air cargo demand over the next decade.

sections.label: Trucker dwell time reduction
sections.summary: The initial phase raised productivity and efficiency, with trucker dwell time reduced by up to 30%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This will raise the productivity and efficiency of current processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And the outcomes from the initial phase have been promising, with dwell time by truckers reduced by up to 30%.

sections.label: Friendly Streets at more locations
sections.summary: Friendly Streets will be launched at 15 more locations island-wide this year, with completion expected by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: These are expected to be completed by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: This year, we will be launching Friendly Streets at 15 more locations island-wide, including in Bukit Timah, Jurong West, Opera Estate, Queenstown, Thomson and Yishun.

sections.label: Enhanced penalties at Friendly Streets
sections.summary: Motorists committing traffic offences that endanger others at Friendly Streets incur two additional demerit points and an additional $100 composition sum.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Motorists who commit traffic offences that endanger others, such as speeding, running of red light or failing to give way to pedestrians at Friendly Streets, will incur two additional demerit points on top of the prevailing demerit points, and an additional $100 in composition sum on top of the prevailing penalties for the offence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: These enhanced penalties will then be on par with offences committed at Silver and School Zones.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We will also extend the lower speed limits for Enhanced School Zones along Primary Schools to full day, instead of only during school arrival and dismissal times.

sections.label: Tanjong Pagar walking and cycling
sections.summary: Roadside parking lots along Tanjong Pagar Road will be repurposed to provide wider footpaths and cycling paths.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We had previously shared that we were working to enhance the walking and cycling experience in Tanjong Pagar.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that after engaging stakeholders in the area, we will repurpose the roadside parking lots along Tanjong Pagar Road to provide wider footpaths and cycling paths.

sections.label: Taxi fleet growth cap suspended
sections.summary: The growth cap on the taxi fleet will continue to be suspended.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: First, we will continue to suspend the growth cap on the taxi fleet.

sections.label: Resale of older taxis
sections.summary: Taxi operators may resell taxis more than three years old, capped at 5% of their fleet annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Third, we will allow taxi operators to resell taxis that are more than three years old, capped at 5% of their fleet annually.

sections.label: Levelling taxis and PHCs
sections.summary: Measures in the PHC sector aim to level the playing field between taxis and PHCs, including a three-year holding period for business-owned chauffeured PHCs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: They complement our moves in the PHC sector to further level the playing field between taxis and PHCs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We announced earlier on 19 February that all newly registered, converted or transferred chauffeured PHCs owned by businesses cannot be converted to other vehicle classifications for three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The main reason for this move is to narrow the regulatory gap between taxis and PHCs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The three-year holding period for business-owned chauffeured PHCs parallels our requirement that taxi operators maintain their taxis for at least three years before they can be resold.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Minister Chee just announced that the Bus Safety Tripartite Taskforce which I chaired has completed its work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: The Government accepted the recommendations of the task force and will work closely with our tripartite partners to implement them over the coming years.

sections.label: Bus collision warning systems
sections.summary: The task force recommended the Government equip buses with 360-degree collision warning, anti-fatigue and camera mirror systems.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: The task force has recommended that the Government equip our buses with 360-degree collision warning, anti-fatigue and camera mirror systems.

sections.label: Reviewing recommended bus technologies
sections.summary: The Government will review the task force's recommended technologies through pilots and study incorporating them into fleets and future bus purchases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: The Government will review the various technologies recommended by the task force through pilots and study the feasibility of incorporating such technologies into existing fleets and making these technologies a requirement for upcoming bus purchases.

sections.label: Bus route runtime limit
sections.summary: LTA has committed to not introducing bus routes with scheduled runtimes exceeding two hours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: LTA has committed to not introducing bus routes with scheduled runtimes exceeding two hours.

sections.label: Industry-wide bus training system
sections.summary: The Government will introduce an industry-wide training point system, as recommended by the task force, covering practices like personalised training and peer support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Some of the good practices we saw, such as more personalised training and peer support, can be more prevalent across the bus sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: I am glad to announce that we will be introducing an industry-wide training point system, as recommended by the task force.

sections.label: Vessel, container and bunker records
sections.summary: Annual vessel arrival tonnage reached 3.11 billion gross tonnage, container throughput crossed 40 million TEUs, and bunker sales hit 54.92 million tonnes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Annual vessel arrival tonnage reached 3.11 billion gross tonnage, and Singapore's container throughput crossed 40 million twenty-foot equivalent units, or TEUs, for the first time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Total bunker sales hit a new record of 54.92 million tonnes, with sales of alternative fuel crossing the one million tonne mark for the first time.

sections.label: Berths operational and scheduled
sections.summary: Eleven berths are operational and seven more are scheduled to commence operations by 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Eleven berths are operational and seven more are scheduled to commence operations by 2027.

sections.label: Maritime innovation test-beds expansion
sections.summary: New maritime solutions will be developed by expanding innovation test-beds and regulatory sandboxes to more port locations for testing remote or autonomous operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: We will facilitate the development of new solutions for the maritime ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: We will be expanding our maritime innovation test-beds and regulatory sandboxes to more locations within the port for testing of new solutions, such as remote or autonomous operations.

sections.label: Technical References for alternative fuels
sections.summary: Technical References for alternative fuels are being developed to give shipping companies better quality and quantity assurance when bunkering alternative fuels in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: To answer Mr Neil Parekh's question, we are taking the lead to develop Technical References for alternative fuels, which provide shipping companies better quality and quantity assurance when bunkering alternative fuels in Singapore.

sections.label: Methanol bunkering standards launch
sections.summary: Two sets of standards for methanol bunkering will be launched in March 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: For methanol bunkering, two sets of standards will be launched in March 2025.

sections.label: Maritime Leadership Programme intake increase
sections.summary: MPA, industries and unions will raise the Maritime Leadership Programme annual intake from about 20 to 25 places to admit leaders from adjacent trading and logistics sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: MPA, together with industries and unions, are doing so at two levels: first, we will groom future leaders of the industry by raising the annual intake of the Maritime Leadership Programme (MLP), from about 20 to 25 places, to admit industry leaders from adjacent trading and logistics sectors.

sections.label: PMA speed limit reduction
sections.summary: The speed limit for riding PMAs on public paths will be reduced from 10 kilometres per hour to six kilometres per hour from the first quarter of 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: First, we intend to reduce the speed limit for riding PMAs on public paths from 10 kilometres per hour to six kilometres per hour, from the first quarter of 2026.

sections.label: PMA dimension restrictions alignment
sections.summary: PMA dimension restrictions on public paths will align with public transport from the first quarter of 2026, limiting width, length, height and laden weight.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Second, we will align the PMA dimension restrictions on public paths with those on public transport, also from the first quarter of 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: This means individuals should not ride a PMA exceeding a width of 70 centimetres, a length of 120 centimetres, a height of 150 centimetres and a laden weight of 300 kilogrammes.

sections.label: PMA speed limit public paths
sections.summary: PMAs with a device speed limit of up to 10 kilometres per hour will be allowed on public paths until end-2028.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We understand that genuine users may own PMAs that can go up to 10 kilometres per hour, based on the current rule.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will allow PMAs with a device speed limit of up to 10 kilometres per hour to be used on public paths until end-2028.

sections.label: Mobility Scooter Assessment implementation
sections.summary: The Assessment for Mobility Scooter will be implemented from the fourth quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: From the fourth quarter of this year, we will implement the Assessment for Mobility Scooter (AMS).

sections.label: AMAP public consultation on commuters
sections.summary: AMAP will consult the public on commuters' safety and mobility needs before recommending to the Government, after which motorised PMD and PAB regulations on public transport will be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: While there has not been any fire incident involving such devices on our trains and buses so far, the safety risk is amplified in such enclosed crowded spaces, with potentially serious consequences to surrounding passengers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: As such, AMAP will be consulting the public on the safety and mobility needs of commuters, before making its recommendations to the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Thereafter, we will review the regulations on motorised PMDs and PABs on public transport.

sections.label: Regulatory framework aligned trains buses
sections.summary: By next year, the regulatory framework against inconsiderate behaviour will be aligned across trains and buses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: By next year, our regulatory framework against inconsiderate behaviour will be aligned across trains and buses.

sections.label: Improvements to interchange stations
sections.summary: Plans are made for improvements to North-South-East-West Line stations becoming interchanges with the Jurong Region Line and Cross Island Line, with works from 2027 to 2032.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Before the Yishun case study is finalised, we have already made plans for improvements to North-South-East-West Line stations that will become interchanges with the upcoming Jurong Region Line and Cross Island Line.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: These include Choa Chu Kang and Boon Lay stations, with works to be completed in 2027; Jurong East station, in 2028; Pasir Ris and Ang Mo Kio stations, in 2030; and Clementi station, in 2032.

sections.label: Tighter PMA rules from 2026
sections.summary: New rules from the first quarter of 2026 make riding a PMA above 6km/h and using or selling oversized PMAs an offence, and require medical need certification for mobility scooter users.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Last year, we announced that the Government had accepted recommendations to tighten regulations on Personal Mobility Aids (PMAs) to curb misuse by able-bodied individuals and ensure that the sale and use of PMAs would be safe and sustainable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We intend to commence the new rules from the first quarter of 2026, to ensure that users and retailers have sufficient time to get used to the new rules.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Based on the new rules, riding a PMA on public paths above a speed of 6km/h and using or selling oversized PMAs will be an offence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: To curb the misuse of mobility scooters, from the first quarter of 2026, users will be required to have a certification of medical need to ride on public paths.

sections.label: Thanks for rail funding speech
sections.summary: A member thanks the Minister for a detailed speech indicating about $1 billion to strengthen rail capabilities and skills upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: First of all, I would like to thank Minister for his very detailed speech earlier, indicating about $1 billion to strengthen rail capabilities and skills upgrading.

sections.label: School surveillance enforcement question
sections.summary: A member asks whether surveillance and monitoring around schools will be enhanced and how 24/7 enforcement will be carried out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: When it comes around that, in terms of enforcement, will there be enhancement in terms of surveillance and monitoring around the schools because it is now going to be 24/7 around the school and how will you enforce that?

sections.label: Bus captain health check-ups
sections.summary: A member asks whether there will be enhancements to regular health check-ups for bus captains or whether this is already under review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Pilots do regular health check-ups, on a regular basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: I was intently hearing your explanation earlier, but I could not sort of capture whether there were any enhancements in terms of check-ups for our bus captains on a regular basis and whether there will be improvements or enhancements for bus captains going forward, or is it already in the plan in terms of the review?

sections.label: Check-ups and certification grants
sections.summary: The speaker says regular check-ups are done through a tripartite mechanism and that those needing certification can apply and receive grants based on means testing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: As far as regular check-ups are concerned, I am personally aware that this is something that is done through the tripartite mechanism with the unions as well as the public transport operators and perhaps, we could look at that area to see what else can be done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: But for those who need to get the certification, they can apply through the current process, they will receive the grants based on the means testing basis.

sections.label: Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme review
sections.summary: The speaker says local situations, ridership and demand must be considered, and will ask LTA colleagues to discuss possible improvements with Mr Ang.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For the Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme, we do need to look at the local situations, the ridership, the demand, but I think based on what Mr Ang has shared, I will certainly ask LTA colleagues to have a good discussion with him and his colleagues to see whether we are able to make some improvements.

sections.label: Autonomous vehicle shuttle pilot routes
sections.summary: The speaker assures union involvement in the pilot and says autonomous vehicle shuttles will start with Service 400, then Service 191 in one-north.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And Ms Yeo Wan Ling has taken over from Mr Yong, and I think that partnership continues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, I want to assure Mr Yong that we will involve the unions closely in this pilot, because we understand that there will be an impact on workers and we want to assure our workers that when we make some of these changes we will bring the workers along with us, and if there are some jobs that will be affected as a result of the implementation of new technologies, we will help our workers to be able to make the transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, we intend to start the deployment of the autonomous vehicle shuttles with routes that are not so challenging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, the first will be Service 400, which serves the Marina Bay South and Shenton Bay area, and the second one is Service 191 in one-north after that.

sections.label: Sustainable aviation fuel and airport
sections.summary: The passage states that sustainability efforts include adopting sustainable aviation fuel, designing T5 as an environmentally sustainable airport, and using technology to improve air traffic management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But as I mentioned in my speech, we also want to make sure that we grow in a sustainable manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And for the second one on sustainability, we will pay attention to a few aspects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Of course, the adoption of sustainable aviation fuel is one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We will look at whether we can ramp up our adoption, moving in tandem with global developments and the availability of supply, because that is one constraint that affects many airlines at the moment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: New investments in production capacity will be needed to be able to increase supply, then to be able to support higher levels of sustainable aviation fuel adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But besides sustainable aviation fuel, we also want to look at how we design the airport – and T5 will incorporate this – to be an environmentally sustainable airport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, the way the airport operates, both the air side operations, and also on the passenger side, how we use energy efficiency measures to reduce energy consumption, to be able to maximise our usage of renewable energy, and also one other aspect which we are looking at is to use technology to improve air traffic management, because if you can reduce the time that the planes are circling and waiting up in the skies, and you can, through that process, reduce fuel consumption, I think that is also another way to be able to help businesses to save cost and reduce carbon emissions.

sections.label: Ten-year validity period
sections.summary: The passage states that when this was implemented, a validity period of 10 years was put in place.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: When we implemented this, we put a validity period of 10 years.

sections.label: Feedback and validity period review
sections.summary: The passage states that feedback from stakeholders and interested parties will continue to be taken in and the validity period's appropriateness monitored, and that a five-year renewal is a concession for owners whose COE was expiring and cannot be renewed again.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We will continue to, as we have done, take in feedback from stakeholders, interested parties and monitor the appropriateness of this validity period.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But having said that, even the two system – 10-year and five-year – the five-year was a concession for owners whose COE was expiring.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: If they renew for five years, they will not be able to renew again.

sections.label: EV battery lifespan check
sections.summary: The passage states that ChatGPT was checked and the lifespan of EV batteries is 10 to 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In fact, I checked ChatGPT too, lifespan of EV batteries is 10 to 20 years.
